column1: Where does the tool flag confusing C/C++ micro-patterns, like the comma operator, embedded increments, or an assignment whose value gets consumed, that are known to make code easy to misread?
Where does the ranker split identifiers into camelCase and snake_case subtokens and score them against a search query using BM25?
Where does the tool turn resolved symbol references into the compressed sparse-row structure used for ranking?
Where is the power-iteration algorithm that assigns each symbol an importance score based on who references it implemented?
Where does the tool narrow an ambiguous method call to its actual receiver's class before falling back to matching every same-named function in the repo?
Where does the tool check for memory-layout anti-patterns, like a vector of raw pointers or a vector of vectors, that hurt data locality?
Where does the tool measure whether a doc comment's words actually add information beyond what the function's own name already says?
Where is the hand-rolled HTTP transport that lets the tool's protocol server be reached remotely, with loopback-only binding and a bearer token by default?
Where does the code live that safely inserts or replaces a named symbol's body in a file, locking it, checking a freshness hash, then writing atomically?
Where does the tool shell out to git to mine per-commit changed-file sets and compute which files tend to change together?
Where does the tool figure out whether an identifier ever existed anywhere in the repository's history, even if it isn't in any file today?
Where does the tool compare several branches pairwise to find which ones touch the same symbols, so it can suggest a safe order to land them?
Where does the tool implement plain literal and regular-expression text matching, scanning every file in parallel instead of maintaining an index?
Where does the tool rank and return the full text of the markdown notes and design docs most relevant to a described task?
Where does the tool pick the single best existing instance of a function or class to imitate, based on complexity and how well-tested and well-used it is, rather than by matching similar text?
Where does the tool check whether a documentation file's references to specific line numbers, symbol names, or counts still hold true against the current code?
Where does the tool work out what code would start running and which tests cover it if a single currently-inactive build flag were turned on?
Where does the tool combine a change's blast radius, the tests that reach it, and the files usually edited alongside it into one after-the-edit report?
Where does the tool read hardware performance counters, such as cycles, instructions, and cache misses, on Apple Silicon and Linux?
Where is the custom sorted associative container, a SIMD-accelerated B+ tree, that stands in for the standard map types the project isn't allowed to use?
